recognize: the light in the scene, as one look: soft side light, golden hour light, a softbox, chiaroscuro.
reader.heading: For light:
reader.text: list, the id of the lighting list for it: "lighting.scene" (light described as light: its quality, direction, color, the time of day) for light in general ("light", "lighting", "soft light", "evening light"); another lighting list below only when the part's words call for that kind of named look ("studio lighting", "dramatic lighting", "neon light", "lamplight").

questions.invalid: part {n}: light list "{value}" is not one of the lighting lists

examples: "lit by ⟦lighting⟧" (keep nothing; category "lighting") -> "soft, warm light falling from one side", "cool, even morning light"
rules: A light describes the light itself: its quality, direction, color and strength, the time of day, the weather. Name a source only when the prompt's own words already have it, or when nearly every such scene has it (the sun or sky outdoors, a window indoors, a candle on a dinner table); never a lamp, screen, sign or fixture the prompt doesn't have, since naming one puts it in the picture: not "light from a streetlamp", "an overhead spotlight", "wall sconces", "a passing car's headlights" or "a TV in the corner", but how the light looks ("cool, even light", "warm light low from one side"). A light core stays light: build on it with where it falls and how it looks on this scene, never with a source for it. The light must suit this exact place and time: no golden-hour sun on a beach indoors, no shade from a tree in a living room. Reject a light idea that this place wouldn't have.
writer.note: This part is the light. Each variant says how the light looks: its quality, direction, color and strength, the time of day or the weather. Name no lamp, fixture, screen, sign, spotlight, sconce, headlight or other source the prompt doesn't already have.

improve: A value that describes the light is the light itself: add no lamp, screen or fixture for it that the request doesn't name.
